scenarios.title: Where You Live
scenarios.text: Half the roster lives in the same glass tower downtown, with a rooftop pool and a doorman who knows everyone's name. The rent is a quarter of your salary.

choices.label: Rent something modest
choices.result: You rent a two-bedroom twenty minutes from the facility, above a bakery. The teammates call it 'the bakery'. You save more in a month than some of them save in a year, and the commute is short.

choices.label: Move into the tower
choices.result: You sign the lease in the tower. The pool parties are legendary, the elevator rides are full of teammates, and the rent comes out of every check like a tax.

choices.label: Room with a teammate
choices.result: You split a place with another rookie. It's cheaper, louder, and you never eat dinner alone.

scenarios.title: Homesick in {town}
scenarios.text: Nobody in {town} knows your name yet, and the apartment is very quiet on Tuesday nights.

choices.label: Call home every night
choices.result: You call home every night for a week. {parent} starts saving up stories for you, like he used to before school.

choices.label: Make the city yours
choices.result: You pick one new neighborhood every Tuesday and walk it until dinner. By October, {town} has a coffee shop that knows your order.

choices.label: Bury it in work
choices.result: You spend every quiet night in the film room. You're the best-prepared rookie on the roster and the loneliest.

choices.label: Keep the Sunday call
choices.result: You kept the Sunday call through four years of college, and you keep it now. The first Sunday in {town}, {sibling} answers and talks for an hour.
choices.lock_text: having promised to call home every week

scenarios.title: The Backup Wants Your Job
scenarios.text: {backup} is on the practice squad and has been kicking very well where the coaches can see.

choices.label: Kick with {backup}
choices.result: You ask {backup} to share your warmups. It makes you both better, and it makes the coaches' decision harder, which is fine.

choices.label: Out-work {backup}
choices.result: You stay later than {backup} every day for a month. The coaches notice the hours more than the kicks.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.result: You decide the practice squad isn't your problem. Your kicking stays the same, and so does the whispering.

scenarios.title: The New Holder Midseason
scenarios.text: {holder} is hurt, and the replacement holder is a backup quarterback who has never held for a kick.

choices.label: Teach the new holder
choices.result: You stay after practice every day with the backup quarterback until the laces spin right. By Friday the holds are clean.

choices.label: Ask for a different holder
choices.result: You ask {coach} for the punter instead. The coach agrees, and the quarterback looks relieved.

choices.label: Visit {holder}
choices.result: You visit {holder} in the training room and bring the new holder along for a lesson. Two holders and a kicker in one cramped room, laughing.

scenarios.title: The Kick Everyone Saw
scenarios.text: A clip of you in a practice-field trick shot, the ball off the crossbar and into a trash can, goes around the league.

choices.label: Make a few more
choices.result: You film a series with the specialists. It's fun, the club's social media team loves it, and the coaches don't.

choices.label: Let it be one clip
choices.result: You thank people and leave it there. It fades in a week.

choices.label: Use it for charity
choices.result: You turn the clip into a charity challenge: a donation for every kid who sends in their own trick shot.

scenarios.title: Contract Year: Prove It
scenarios.text: It's the last year of your rookie deal, and the front office wants to see one more season before it talks.

choices.label: Put your head down
choices.result: You stop reading anything about contracts and kick. Your agent handles the rest, and the season feels lighter for it.

choices.label: Ask {coach} what they want
choices.result: You ask {coach} exactly what the club needs from you this year. The answer is two things, and both are fixable.

choices.label: Push for a deal now
choices.result: You have your agent push for an extension before the season. The club says no, politely, and remembers that you asked.

scenarios.title: The Quarterback's Ego
scenarios.text: The franchise quarterback blames the special teams in a press conference, and the reporters come to your locker next.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.result: You say you're focused on your job and leave it there. The quarterback notices, and so does the locker room.

choices.label: Fire back
choices.result: You say the special teams aren't the problem. It's the clip of the week, and the quarterback stops talking to you.

choices.label: Talk to him privately
choices.result: You find him at his locker after practice and ask what he actually meant. It turns out he was angry at himself. He says so at the next press conference.

scenarios.title: The Owner's Gala
scenarios.text: Black tie, the owner's charity gala, and a donor who wants a photo and then a favor: a visit to his company's party next week.

choices.label: Take the photo, skip the favor
choices.result: You smile for the photo and say your schedule is full. He's disappointed and forgets about it by dessert.

choices.label: Do the favor
choices.result: You show up at his company party. It's two hours of handshakes and a check for the gala's charity with your name on it.

choices.label: Leave early
choices.result: You stay an hour and slip out before the auction. Nobody asks for anything, and you're asleep by ten.

scenarios.title: The Specialists' Dinner
scenarios.text: The kicker, the punter and the snapper have a weekly dinner. A new punter wants in, and the other two are looking at you.

choices.label: Invite the new punter
choices.result: You invite the new punter. Four is louder than three, and the dinner gets better.

choices.label: Keep it to three
choices.result: You say the dinner is for three and leave it there. It stays easy, and the new punter eats alone that month.

choices.label: Make it a unit dinner
choices.result: You invite the whole special teams unit. It's chaos, and it's the best night of the season.

scenarios.title: The Trick Play
scenarios.text: The new coordinator wants a fake field goal with you throwing the pass, and you haven't thrown a ball since high school.

choices.label: Practice the throw
choices.result: You throw fifty passes a day for a week until the ball stops wobbling. The coordinator puts it in the playbook.

choices.label: Ask for a different fake
choices.result: You suggest a fake where the holder runs and you just block. The coordinator likes it better.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.result: You laugh and say you're a kicker. The coordinator doesn't laugh, and the fake goes to the punter.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Slump
scenarios.text: Your first real slump, and every veteran in the room has a theory about your plant foot.

choices.label: Listen to one person
choices.result: You pick the one voice you trust, {coach}, and tune out the rest. The fix is small and it takes.

choices.label: Try every theory
choices.result: You try every veteran's advice in one week. Your form is a mess, and your confidence is worse.

choices.label: Kick until it comes back
choices.result: You kick two hundred balls a day until something clicks. Your leg is sore, and the slump breaks.

choices.label: Call someone who helped before
choices.result: You call the people who helped the last time you struggled, and the plan you made then still works.

scenarios.title: The Rookie on a Run
scenarios.text: The streak is a month old, and the rookie card companies are calling your agent.

choices.label: Don't talk about it
choices.result: You don't say a word about the streak, and neither does anyone in the specialists' room.

choices.label: Enjoy the attention
choices.result: You do the interviews, the card shoot and a podcast. It's fun, and you're tired by Friday.

choices.label: Credit the unit
choices.result: Every interview is about the snapper and {holder}. The specialists' group chat is very happy.

scenarios.title: The Veteran They Signed to Push You
scenarios.text: The club signs a thirty-four-year-old kicker 'for depth'. Everybody knows what that means for a rookie.

choices.label: Learn from the veteran
choices.result: You ask the veteran to watch your warmup. He does, and fixes something in five minutes.

choices.label: Compete every day
choices.result: You turn every practice into a contest. The veteran is tired by October, and you aren't.

choices.label: Go out and forget about it
choices.result: You go out with the other rookies every night that week to stop thinking about the veteran. It works until Monday, when {coach} notices you look tired.
